summary: Point Sherman Light on Lynn Canal, first lit 1904 and given to the Forest Service in 1932; a 1981 day marker and light now stand on the site.

structures.note: White hexagonal tower with black hexagonal lantern room (LHF). Whether this 1904 tower still stands is not stated in the sources read.
One-and-one-half-story keeper's dwelling east of the light (LHF; USLHS). Destroyed in the 1940s by a fire set by a caretaker (marker; no year given).
Stood just east of the light (LHF; USLHS).
Checkerboard day marker and light placed on the site of the original light; operated by the US Coast Guard (CoastView).

access.note: Grounds and dwelling closed; the archive lists the station as not open to the public (LHF; USLHS).

visit.note: Visible from cruise ships and ferries in Lynn Canal (LHF).

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner per LHF; Forest Service held the station from 1932 per LHF)

events.note: Built during the summer of 1904 with hired labor (LHF).
Andrew Jackson, first principal keeper (USLHS roster; LHF).
David H. Somerville, principal keeper 1909-1911 (USLHS roster).
Two keepers of the Eldred Rock light drowned in a small sail boat between Eldred Rock and Point Sherman, reported in the Skagway paper of 31 March 1910. Not a Point Sherman keeper.
Fixed white oil light replaced by an acetylene light showing a white flash every three seconds; focal plane raised from 38 ft to 42 ft (LHF; CoastView).
Light automated; last resident keeper withdrawn (LHF; CoastView).
Station transferred to the Forest Service and replaced by a nearby buoy (LHF; CoastView).
Archive: year discontinued 1932. Marker says disestablished before 1917 (see conflicts).
Day marker and light placed on the site of the original light; operated by the US Coast Guard (CoastView; LHF).

keepers.name: Andrew Jackson
keepers.note: First keeper of the light (LHF). 10 November 1907 garden report printed by LHF.

wrecks.vessel: small sail boat (unnamed) with two Eldred Rock keepers, Adams and Scotty Curran
wrecks.outcome: Both men drowned somewhere between Eldred Rock and Point Sherman (Skagway paper, 31 March 1910). An overturned boat was sighted drifting off Sherman point. Not a Point Sherman keeper; the paper's 'last Tuesday' is taken to mean 29 March 1910.

corrections.why: The archive records the light at 38 feet above mean high water (11.6 m) for the original station; LHF and CoastView agree on 38 feet before 1911. The record's 3.0 m matches neither this nor the tower's 6 ft (1.8 m). After the 1911 change CoastView gives 42 ft (12.8 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The marker gives 38 statute miles north of Juneau; CoastView gives 46 statute miles north-west. Both are kept in the story; the record has no distance field to resolve.

LHF and CoastView agree on a fixed white oil light until 1911, then an acetylene light flashing white every three seconds with a raised focal plane. The marker's acetylene lantern for the original optic conflicts and is not used.

notes_for_editor: Moderate station: five sources, two of them secondary (LHF, CoastView) and one a marker. Roster is the four USLHS lines, copied as printed. Open conflicts left for an editor: (1) Date the light was given up: the record's 1917 (Wikidata) and the marker's 'before 1917' against the archive's and LHF's 1932; no source read explains the 1917 date, so the story gives both. (2) Original optic: the marker says acetylene lantern; LHF and CoastView say fixed white oil until 1911. (3) Distance from Juneau: marker 38 statute miles north; CoastView 46 statute miles north-west. (4) Rank: LHF calls Richard W. Meade 'Captain' and CoastView 'Commander'; the story says 'naval officer'. The 1869 naming date comes from CoastView only; alaska.guide and alaskahandbook.com were blocked (HTTP 307 and 429), and anyplaceamerica.com returned 403, so the place-name record (Orth) was not checked. The 1907 garden report is known only through LHF's printed text; the original was not read. The 1940s fire is undated; the events list does not give a year for it. Chronicling America searches found no Point Sherman news from 1904 to 1911 (the 16 hits were mostly unrelated); the 1910 Eldred Rock drowning is the one relevant newspaper item. The Lighthouse Board volumes in the corpus are dated 1891 to 1901 and the Commissioner's 1915 index lists Point Sherman among Alaska stations, which was not used because it is only an index entry. A 1901 Lighthouse Board entry for 'Sherman Rock bell buoy' in Lynn Canal is a different aid and was not used. Wikipedia was used for leads only and is not cited; the Wikipedia article gives 1917 for 'reduced to a minor light' but that is not sourced here. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1910 Daily Alaskan page was read directly (Eldred Rock keepers, 'last Tuesday', the overturned boat off Sherman point); the marker's 'destroyed in the 1940s' sentence and 'before 1917' were checked against the marker text. The story now says the 1896-1899 traffic put a run of lighthouses along the Inside Passage (CoastView's words), not along Lynn Canal. The 47 ft focal plane and the diamond day marker are CoastView's; the 38/42 ft figures are CoastView's and the archive's. The roster roles (principal, acting principal) are as the USLHS record prints them; 'first keeper' is LHF's word and is now cited to LHF as well.
